question: Did the Israelites kill every male in Midian?
summary: Numbers 31:7 reports the Israelites killed all the males of Midian, and verses 17-18 instruct them to kill every remaining male child plus every non-virgin woman. Yet Judges 6 opens with the Midianites oppressing Israel for seven years, swarming up 'as grasshoppers for multitude.' If every Midianite male was slaughtered in Numbers, where did the Judges 6 horde come from?

reconcile.connective: Defenders read Numbers 31 as a limited, local slaughter of the Midianites near the camp, leaving large numbers who fled or were absent to reemerge in Judges 6.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells presses the inconsistency directly: if every Midianite male was killed under Moses, the swarming horde of Judges 6 cannot exist two centuries later.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (2013; online edition)

pd_work.resource: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown, Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible (1871)
pd_work.author: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown
pd_work.note: JFB treats this passage directly, arguing the Numbers 31 destruction was 'only partial' and expressly comparing Judges 6:1 to explain the Midianites' survival into the period of the Judges.

link.note: No allowlisted page treats this specific Numbers 31 / Judges 6 reappearance contradiction; the defendinginerrancy.com Numbers 31 page addresses only the moral problem, so no link is supplied.

excerpts.excerpt_text: But the destruction appears to have been only partial—limited to those who were in the neighborhood of the Hebrew camp and who had been accomplices in the villainous plot of Baal-peor (Num 25:1-3), while a large portion of the Midianites were absent on their pastoral wanderings or had saved themselves by flight. (Compare Jdg 6:1).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers the contradiction: the Num 31 slaughter was 'only partial,' local to the camp, and explicitly cross-references Jdg 6:1 to account for the surviving Midianites of Judges.
